title: Grade 4 Math — Fri, Jun 27
description: Data Handling — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — tally, pictograph and bar graph
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A pictograph has key: 🌸 = 3 flowers. A row shows 4🌸 and ½🌸. How many flowers?
Bar graph: y-axis 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. A bar reaches the 15 mark. The value is:
questions.explanation: The bar reaches the '15' mark on the y-axis. Value = 15.

questions.question: Which of these is a CORRECT statement about data handling?
options: A bar graph and a pictograph always show different data
Both pictographs and bar graphs represent the same data but in different visual formats — bar graphs give more precise readings
Tally marks are more accurate than bar graphs
You cannot convert tally marks to a bar graph
questions.explanation: The SAME data can be displayed as a tally chart, pictograph or bar graph. Each format has advantages. Bar graphs allow more precise readings. Pictographs are more visual and engaging.

questions.question: Survey result: Dogs: 12, Cats: 8, Birds: 4. Total number of pets recorded:
Pictograph: Votes for colour. Red: 🔴🔴🔴, Blue: 🔴🔴🔴🔴🔴, Green: 🔴🔴. Key = 4 votes per symbol. How many votes did Blue get?
Data: A=20, B=35, C=15, D=30. If you make a bar graph with scale 5, how many marks are on the y-axis (including 0)?
A student is given data: cricket fans=50, football fans=30, badminton fans=20. Which BEST scale would she use for a pictograph?
questions.explanation: Scale=10: cricket=5, football=3, badminton=2 symbols. Clean, whole numbers. Scale=1 = 100 symbols total (too many). Scale=100 = fractions. Scale=10 is ideal.

questions.question: Data table: Months | Books sold. Jan=40, Feb=30, Mar=50, Apr=20. Which month had the LEAST sales?
questions.explanation: April = 20 (the smallest value). April had the least books sold.

questions.question: Bar graph analysis: Runs scored by 4 batsmen. A=60, B=40, C=75, D=25. What fraction of the total did batsman C score?
questions.explanation: A=60, B=40, C=75, D=25. Total = 200. C scored 75 runs. Fraction = 75/200 = 3/8 of total runs.

questions.question: A class makes a frequency table of birthdays per month. January has 3 birthdays, June has 5, December has 2. Which question can the table answer?
options: In which month were the most students born?
In which year were students born?
questions.explanation: A frequency table answers 'how many' per category. 'Which month had most birthdays?' = June (5). It cannot give individual names, birth order or years — only category counts.

questions.question: Pictograph vs Bar graph: 'I need to show exact values like 37, 43, 29, 51.' Which is BETTER for this data?
options: Bar graph (height on a numerical scale shows exact values)
questions.explanation: Bar graphs show exact values on a numbered y-axis — a bar can reach any height precisely. Pictographs struggle with numbers that aren't multiples of the key (37 = 3.7 symbols on a scale of 10 — awkward).

questions.question: The data says: Class 4A scored an average of 75 marks. Class 4B scored 70. Class 4C scored 80. Which class had the HIGHEST average? How much higher than the lowest?
questions.explanation: Highest = Class 4C (80). Lowest = Class 4B (70). 80 − 70 = 10 marks higher.

questions.question: Data: Weather type in June. Sunny: |||| |||| ||||, Cloudy: |||| ||||, Rainy: |||| ||. How many MORE sunny days than rainy days?
questions.explanation: Sunny = 15 (3 groups of 5). Rainy = 7 (5+2). 15 − 7 = 8 more sunny days.

questions.question: True or False: 'A graph is only useful when it is big and colourful.' Explain.
options: True — colour and size make data clearer
False — a graph's usefulness comes from accurate data, a clear scale, proper labels and a title. A small, simple, well-labelled graph beats a large, colourful but misleading one.
True — only coloured graphs are accepted in exams
questions.explanation: A graph's value = accuracy + clarity of labels + correct scale + informative title. Colour and size can help but are not the measure of quality. A misleading graph with beautiful colours is harmful.
